rows.text: I’d be pretty likely to sign up, like a 7–8/10, because I’m anxious about my blood pressure creeping back up and I don’t want to regain after coming off compounded semaglutide. $99/month feels reasonable compared to the $349 branded meds and even what I was paying before, and I like the idea of tracking ApoB and having direct messaging. My hesitation is whether the coronary calcium score is actually included or if that’s an extra out-of-pocket test, and I’d want to know if they’ll also help with weight maintenance (not just labs) since that’s my biggest fear right now.

I’d say I’m moderately likely—maybe a 6 or 7 out of 10—because the family history piece hits really close to home and I like that it’s a real physician, not a wellness influencer. My hesitation is the $99/month on top of what I already pay for insurance through the district, and I’d want to know what the coronary calcium scan costs and whether I’d end up paying extra for labs/meds. Also, “manages them down” sounds good, but I’d need to be sure it’s practical for someone busy and that they’re not just selling supplements or generic advice I could get from my primary care doctor.

I’d be moderately likely, like a 6 or 7 out of 10, because the family history part hits close to home and I don’t want to end up like my dad or brother. My hesitation is the “no insurance needed” piece—$99/month adds up fast on a teacher budget, and I’d want to know what’s included (especially the coronary calcium scan cost) and whether they’d coordinate with my regular doctor. I’m also a little wary of anything that feels like a wellness program in disguise, but if it’s truly physician-led with clear lab/scan pricing and real follow-up, I’d seriously consider it.

I’d be somewhat likely, maybe a 6 or 7 out of 10, just because heart stuff really freaks me out with my dad and my brother, and I like that it’s a real physician and not some wellness program. The $99/month adds up, though, and I’d want to know what’s actually included (labs, the coronary calcium scan, meds, follow-ups) and whether they’ll coordinate with my primary care so I’m not paying twice through my district insurance. I also worry about getting pushed into a bunch of extra tests or supplements, and I’d need it to be genuinely convenient since I’m busy during the school year.

I’d say moderately likely—maybe a 6 or 7 out of 10—because with a calcium score of 280 I’m not thrilled with “we’ll keep an eye on it,” and I’d pay to get a real plan and tighter follow-up than my 12‑minute PCP visits. $99/month is in the “annoying but doable” range, and I have HSA money, but I’d hesitate until I knew exactly what “manages them down” means (meds? statin/ezetimibe/PCSK9? BP targets?) and whether labs/imaging are extra. I’d also want to know the physician’s credentials, response times on messaging, and how they coordinate with local testing in Michigan—otherwise it risks feeling like a subscription for advice I can already get, just faster.

I’d say I’m moderately likely—maybe a 6–7 out of 10—because my calcium score is 280 and “we’ll keep an eye on it” doesn’t feel like a plan. I like the idea of actually tracking ApoB and blood pressure with someone who’ll adjust meds and follow up without me begging for another 12‑minute appointment, and $99/month is reasonable if it’s truly hands-on and HSA-eligible. My hesitation is whether it’s real medical management (statins, BP meds, labs ordered, action thresholds) versus generic coaching, and whether they’ll coordinate with my local PCP and handle prescriptions and imaging orders in Michigan. I’d also want to know what’s included—how often labs, how quickly messaging replies, and if the $99 is on top of lab costs or if they’re bundled.

I’d say I’m moderately likely—maybe a 6 or 7 out of 10—because my calcium score is 280 and “we’ll keep an eye on it” isn’t a plan, and I’m tired of 12-minute visits. My hesitation is whether this is real medical management (meds, targets, follow-up intervals, coordination with labs/imaging) or just coaching with nice dashboards, and I’d want to know who the physician is and what the protocol is if my numbers don’t improve. Also, I’d want clarity on whether labs/imaging are included or out-of-pocket on top, because with a high deductible that can add up fast.

I’d say moderately likely—maybe a 6 or 7 out of 10—because $99/month is way more doable than the $349 I’m staring at now, and I’m genuinely worried my blood pressure is creeping back up if I regain. My hesitation is whether that price really includes the labs/scans or if I’m going to get hit with extra costs for the calcium score, and also whether they’d help me with weight management meds or it’s more “education” than actual treatment. If it felt like real ongoing management and not a bait-and-switch on testing costs, I’d probably try it.

If my wife stayed on me and they were upfront about total costs (especially that coronary calcium scan), I’d be more likely.
